tests.name: Urine Protein
tests.plain_english: Protein in urine can indicate that the kidneys are not filtering blood properly.
tests.low_means: No protein detected is the normal, healthy result.
tests.high_means: Protein in urine may indicate kidney disease, urinary tract infection, or high blood pressure affecting the kidneys.

tests.name: Urine Glucose
tests.plain_english: Glucose should not normally appear in urine. Its presence suggests blood sugar may be very high.
tests.low_means: No glucose in urine is normal.
tests.high_means: Glucose in urine may indicate uncontrolled diabetes.

tests.name: Urine pH
tests.plain_english: Urine pH measures how acidic or alkaline your urine is, which can reflect your diet and kidney function.
tests.low_means: Very acidic urine may indicate a high-protein diet or certain metabolic conditions.
tests.high_means: Very alkaline urine may indicate a urinary tract infection or kidney issues.

tests.name: Urine Leukocytes
tests.plain_english: White blood cells in urine can indicate a urinary tract infection or kidney inflammation.
tests.low_means: No leukocytes in urine is the normal result.
tests.high_means: Leukocytes in urine suggest infection or inflammation in the urinary tract.

tests.name: Urine Nitrites
tests.plain_english: Nitrites in urine are produced by certain bacteria and are a sign of bacterial infection.
tests.low_means: No nitrites is the normal, healthy result.
tests.high_means: Nitrites present suggests a bacterial urinary tract infection.

tests.name: Urine Ketones
tests.plain_english: Ketones are produced when your body burns fat for energy instead of glucose.
tests.low_means: No ketones is the normal result for most people.
tests.high_means: High ketones may indicate uncontrolled diabetes, prolonged fasting, or a very low carbohydrate diet.
